newsitem.title: USA: Virginia executes murderer of state trooper.
newsitem.headline: Virginia executes murderer of state trooper.

text.p: A man who admitted killing a state trooper after being stopped for driving a stolen car in 1985 was executed by lethal injection Tuesday.
Gregory Beaver, 32, was pronounced dead at 9:11 p.m. EST. He was the fifth person executed in Virgina this year and the 34th since executions resumed in the state in 1982.
His last words were, "I love you, Vickie. I'll go to a better place," a prison spokesman said. Vickie was Beaver's wife.

The Supreme Court turned down Beaver's request for a stay of execution in a 6-3 vote Monday leaving Gov. George Allen as his only hope. Allen announced Tuesday afternoon he would not interfere with the sentence.
Beaver pleaded guilty to shooting state trooper Leo Whitt in April 1985 during a traffic stop on Interstate 95 in rural Prince George County.

Beaver had escaped a Maryland drug treatment programme and was in a stolen car. He was returning to Maryland from Florida when Whitt stopped him. He was captured near Richmond not long after the slaying.

His lawyer, Christopher McMurray, had asked Allen to commute the sentence because one of Beaver's trial lawyers was a part-time prosecutor. His other lawyer has since had his license suspended for neglecting clients.

Beaver spent his last day visiting with his family and clergy at the Greensville Correctional Centre, home to Virginia's execution chamber. He ordered a sausage pizza, french fries, and Pepsi for his last meal.

Reached by telephone on Monday, he said, "the most painful thing about all this is not what they can do to me, but what's happening to my family, which, of course, makes me think of what happened to the police officer's family 11 years ago.
"I had a hard time even imagining how much pain they would be going through. Now I know because I see it in my family's eyes," Beaver said.

Four more killers have execution dates in Virginia before Christmas. According to Amnesty International, the state could lead the nation in executions for 1996. South Carolina, with six, now leads the United States this year.

Texas leads the country with 107 executions to date but just three this year. Florida has had 37 to date and seven this year, according to Richard Dieter at the Death Penalty Information Centre in Washington.
